newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight enquiry cited, Iran features.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight enquiry cited, Iran features.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh enquiry on Monday, boosted by the emergence of last week's reported purchases by Iran as freight orders, shipbrokers said on Monday.

Iran was reported as recently having bought at least six cargoes of sugar, with raws for January shipment and whites for March. Possible origins for the whites are Europe and Thailand, while Cuba and Brazil could be departure points for the raws. Secretan's recent order for north Brazil/Iran was still open, but Masters Shipbroking was open on account for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Dunkirk to Iran for prompt/15 December.

E D & F Man was in the market for a prompt 12,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar to Syria from Gdynia or Gdansk with option of Hamburg/Rouen range and also for 12,000 tonnes from Thailand to south China including Hong Kong for 1/5 January.

Cargill was open for 11/14,000 tonnes bagged/bulk from Thailand to Indonesia or the Philippines for the end of December and for 18,388 tonnes min/max in bulk from Recife or Maceio to US Gulf/Atlantic.

Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 12,000 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Indonesia for 5/15 January and was still open for 12/14,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to Med/west Africa for 28 December/10 January.

Louis Dreyfus quoted for 15,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Buenaventura to Sri Lanka/east Africa for 1/6 January and a further 7,000 tonnes, again in bags, from Antwerp/Hamburg to Algeria for 10/20 December or later.
Dreyfus was also said to have fixed 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to US Gulf for 10/16 December at around $17.00.

CSR quoted for 27,000 tonnes in bulk from Queensland to Inchon for 5/15 January and C.Czarnikow for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to east Africa with options of Colombo/Pakistan/Bangladesh.
Secretan was in the market for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo for 5/15 January, while its two earlier north Brazilian orders were said to be still open.
Amerop quoted for 11/12,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to Sri Lanka with options for east Africa, Madagascar, Indonesia and Bangladesh for the second half of December.
Shipbrokers cited a number of account orders from mixed origins to boost the day's new business.

BMM quoted a Space Enterprises account inquiry for 12,500 tonnes in bulk from Kandla to Novorossisk for 25/30 December Charterhouse cited a direct charterer's interest to ship 15/18,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Guangzhou or Huangpu to Karachi for spot/prompt. Its earlier bagged order for 12/13,000 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo was said to be fully firm.

Shyvers Savoy was open on account for 12,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from the Reunion port of Pointe des Galets to Marseilles for 1/5 January. David Bruce cited an account order for 10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to Egyptian Mediterranean for spot/prompt.
Elsewhere, Pakistan has delayed a decision on bids received for the import of 50,000 tonnes of sugar by December 31. Pakistan issued a tender because of the delayed start of the cane crushing season.
